findings.title: `pipeline_mutates` does not inspect `fan_out`'s `inner` step, so that shape skips the run lock
findings.description: `_step_mutates` only recurses into `config.get("steps")` (the `each`/`loop` body shape). A `fan_out` step nests its body under `config["inner"]` (a single-key dict), which is never scanned. If a user-authored pipeline has `fan_out: { inner: { branch: {...} } }` (or `implement`/`devlog`/`commit`-producing inner), `pipeline_mutates` returns `False`, so `_take_run_lock` never acquires the lock even though the fan-out branches mutate git/cf state concurrently. This is a false-negative in the D11 safety gate's own stated scope ("whether any step, **nested steps included**, commits or moves cf state"). No shipped pipeline uses `fan_out` (confirmed against `src/squadron/data/pipelines/*.yaml`), so it is latent, but the detector should treat `inner` as a nesting point it walks, matching how `fan_out.py`/`_execute_fan_out_step` actually run the inner step. There is also no test covering a mutating `fan_out` inner.

findings.title: A per-item report write failure aborts a batch with an uncaught `OSError`
findings.description: The new `await _write_each_report(report, runs_dir, final=False)` after each item is not wrapped in `try/except OSError`. `_write_atomic` logs at ERROR and re-raises, so a disk-full / permission error mid-batch now propagates out of the `each` loop and out of `execute_pipeline` as a raw traceback in the regular (non-item-resume) run path. This is acceptable under fail-fast and is observable (the ERROR log), but it is a coarser failure surface than the cleanly-reported git faults elsewhere in the same step; consider converting a report-write fault into a flagged/halted run state rather than an unhandled exception. This extends pre-existing behavior (the final write was already unguarded on the success path) rather than introducing a new crash on the happy path.

findings.title: Item-resume maps the runner's `typer.Exit` (classification failure) to `HALTED` (3)
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` catches any `typer.Exit` raised by `_run_pipeline_sdk` and re-raises as `ResumeExit.HALTED`. `GitEnvironmentError` is correctly re-raised by the runner for the item path (verified at `run.py:398`), but `ClassificationError` and `LazySessionConnectError` are converted to `typer.Exit(1)` *inside* `_run_pipeline_sdk` before this catch, so both end up reported as `HALTED` ("an environment fault or unknown git state ended it mid-item"). A classification failure is closer to `REJECTED` ("nothing ran"). This is a minor exit-code-precision issue for automated callers (D8 treats the code as a contract); it does not lose data, since the body never ran.

findings.title: `report.json` round-trip, reserved-param enforcement, and dependency ordering are consistent and well-tested
findings.description: Verified against the tests: `to_json`/`from_json` round-trip with `StrEnum` values serialized by their value (`json.dumps` on a `StrEnum` subclass yields the value string; `from_json` re-coerces via `FlagKind(str(...))`). `BatchReport.load` validates `schemaVersion` and wraps all parse failures in `BatchReportLoadError` with the path named. `reserved_param_error` is the single source for the two control keys and is enforced at all three param entry points (`_apply_param_overrides`, `validate_pipeline`, `item_params`). `order_by_dependencies`/`_find_cycle` terminate on a finite unplaced set and always return a real cycle path; the `not_run`/dependency pre-flag bookkeeping in `_execute_each_step` is consistent with `_pre_flag`/`_flag_kind`. Atomic write-then-replace plus the `list_runs` filter on `REPORT_JSON_SUFFIX` keep report files from being misread as run state.
